result.text: Title: Find a Job You have to regularly report, to which companies you wrote job applications.
Based on your job applications, new potential job offers are sent to you.
Companies have to confirm that they received job applications and rate the application.
A job interview can be negotiated.
When a company wants you to work for them, you enter the probation phase.
After probation phase, you can rate the company and the company can rate you.
Reviews for a company can only be seen (by job applicants) after 1 year.
If a job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless you rated the company C or less, then you continue to receive job offers, but no longer have to report.

Title: Find a Job

After probation phase, you can rate the company and the company can rate you.

If a job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless you rated the company C or less, then you continue to receive job offers, but no longer have to report.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

result.rule: When the description distinguishes activities or outcomes by their action, object, recipient, or stage: Use BPMN labels that preserve those stated distinctions rather than substituting a different action or outcome.

When the description explicitly states an action performed by a participant, and a related receipt or outcome could be mistaken for that action: Label the BPMN activity with the stated action and preserve its direction; do not replace it with the corresponding action from another participant’s perspective.

When the description explicitly states an activity’s action, object, recipient, or multiple coordinated actions: Preserve those stated details in the BPMN task label rather than omitting or substituting them.

When the description distinguishes a participant’s instruction or assignment from the work that another participant is asked to perform: Label the BPMN activity as the instruction or assignment, preserving who directs whom; do not label it as though the directing participant were ordering or performing the requested work.
